newsitem.title: USA: Freighter moved from New Orleans accident site.
newsitem.headline: Freighter moved from New Orleans accident site.

text.p: The crippled freighter that slammed into a popular shopping mall on the banks of the Mississippi River last month was pulled free from the damaged wharf Monday, the Coast Guard said.
More than 100 people were injured when the M/V Bright Field, carrying 64,000 tons of corn, lost power and plowed into the Riverwalk shopping area on Dec. 14.

Coast Guard officer Patrick Cuty told Reuters that fears more of the wrecked shopping center would topple into the river were unfounded. "Not a brick, not even a feather moved off that structure when the ship was pulled out," he said.
The freighter was guided 18 miles (30 km) downriver by six tugs for repairs in a two-hour operation, completed at 4:20 p.m. CST, he said.

Since the accident, tugs held the freighter in place, pushed up against the damaged wharf. The bow of the ship had been aground on the Mississippi River bank beneath the Poydras Street Wharf near the city's historic French Quarter.

He said the ship's engines were idling, but the tugs provided the power for the downriver trip. The river was closed briefly to traffic as the crippled 735-foot (224 metre) freighter backed away from the wharf. Barges were moved in to help support the sagging Riverwalk.
A Coast Guard Board investigation is still working to determine the cause of the accident.
